title: Highest temperature in London on September 7?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Met Office and model guidance (including GFS and ECMWF runs) point to a daytime high of 23–24°C in London on September 7, driven by moderate westerly winds, increasing cloud cover, and limited daytime heating following a sunnier, warmer September 6. These conditions align with the market’s strong consensus on 24°C (52% implied probability) and 25°C (26.5%), well above the long-term September average high of 20.2°C at Heathrow. Forecasters note typical model spread of 1–2°C for 24-hour outlooks, with resolution hinging on exact afternoon maxima and any localized clearing. Updated guidance from the Met Office or new model runs tomorrow morning will likely be the next key input for traders.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models, including GFS outputs, indicate a high of 28–29°C in Paris on September 7 under partly cloudy skies with moderate westerly winds and minimal precipitation risk. This aligns with the market's strong implied probability for 28°C, driven by consistent afternoon peaks near 29°C in ensemble guidance and above the 1991–2020 average high of 22.7°C. Stable atmospheric conditions following a similarly warm September 6 have limited upside potential beyond 30°C, while overnight lows near 17–20°C support modest daytime recovery without exceeding recent model consensus. Updated runs overnight or early morning on September 7 remain the key near-term data points for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent rain and thunderstorms forecast for Tokyo on September 7 are limiting daytime heating, keeping the highest temperature tightly clustered around 26–28°C according to Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models. Southerly flow advects humid maritime air while thick cloud cover and heavy precipitation reduce solar insolation, preventing the stronger warming seen on clearer September days. Historical early-September normals near 27–28°C provide a baseline, but current synoptic conditions favor the lower end of that range. Model spreads in rainfall timing and intensity create the narrow probability gap between 27°C and 28°C, with final official observations resolving the market.

Historical September 7 averages near 32.6°C and a 35.2°C record provide context, yet current conditions—low wind speeds, elevated dew points near 24°C, and urban heat retention—support readings several degrees above climatology. Minor model spread arises from timing of residual cloud cover or scattered convection, which could cap the peak near 34°C or permit a brief push toward 36°C before any afternoon showers develop. This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zhcc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This aligns with the market-implied 60.5% probability for 32°C or higher, reflecting trader assessment of stable late-summer warmth before a cooler northeast flow and rain arrive on September 8. Historical September averages near 28–30°C provide context, but recent model runs show limited cooling overnight and daytime heating consistent with highs at or above the 32°C threshold. Official observations from local stations will resolve the market once finalized.
